title: AI Product Experiment Design and Feedback Analytics

questions.question: What should an AI product experiment define before rollout?
options: A demo script that shows the impressive output to stakeholders
A backlog label and a rollout date with no success metric
A hypothesis, success metric, feedback sample, and stop rule
A feedback sample only, collected after the rollout is live
questions.explanation: A product experiment needs a decision structure, not just an implementation idea.

questions.question: Why is an unclear hypothesis a risk?
options: The stop rule becomes the only artifact the team needs
The feedback sample can be collected without any bias review
The team cannot tell what it is trying to learn or measure
The rollout risk note replaces the need for a hypothesis
questions.explanation: Without a hypothesis, feedback cannot be interpreted against a learning goal.

questions.question: What does a stop rule prevent?
options: Collecting a feedback sample before the pilot begins running
Defining a success metric while the experiment is being designed
Scaling weak evidence or harmful behavior into a full rollout
All user research conducted before an AI experiment starts
questions.explanation: A stop rule defines when the team should halt instead of scaling the idea.

questions.question: Which input helps AI feedback synthesis stay credible?
options: Unlabeled anecdotes collected without any stated sample size
A visible feedback sample paired with an explicit bias note
A hidden prompt that stakeholders cannot review or audit
A single executive quote presented as the full user feedback view
questions.explanation: The team needs to understand where the feedback came from and what bias it may contain.

questions.question: Which product idea is most ready for a controlled experiment?
options: One with no user segment and no plan for a feedback sample
One with no decision owner and no defined stop rule for the pilot
One with user feedback, a clear metric, and known rollout risk
One with no success metric and an undefined hypothesis statement
questions.explanation: Feedback, metric clarity, and known risk are good reasons to run a controlled experiment.

questions.question: What should AI assist with in feedback analytics?
options: Replacing the product team rollout and stop-rule decisions
Hiding negative feedback that contradicts the stated hypothesis
Removing the need for a success metric before the rollout decision
Synthesizing feedback while decisions stay under human review
questions.explanation: AI can help synthesize feedback, but product decisions still need human review and evidence.
